_medtap_comment: Piru's one-sentence mechanism line (target + action, at most 25 words) for each MedTAP record whose label prose Piru ships in its place, keyed by MedTAP record name and emitted as a `piru-curated` `mechanisms_summary` row. Derived from that record's mechanismOfAction.summary; a record whose summary states no molecular mechanism has no key here. pipeline/audit/claim_language.py gates every line.

medtap_lines.acalabrutinib: Covalent inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase, blocking B-cell antigen receptor and cytokine receptor signaling.
medtap_lines.Amphetamine: Blocks norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake into the presynaptic neuron and increases their release into the extraneuronal space.
medtap_lines.Anastrozole: Selective non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, lowering conversion of adrenal androgens to estrone and estradiol.
medtap_lines.Arformoterol: The (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol, a selective long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist.
medtap_lines.Asparaginase: Catalyzes deamidation of asparagine to aspartic acid and ammonia, lowering circulating asparagine.
medtap_lines.Atomoxetine: Selective inhibitor of the presynaptic norepinephrine transporter.
medtap_lines.Atropine: Reversible antagonist at muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, without distinguishing the M1, M2 and M3 subgroups.
medtap_lines.Balsalazide: A prodrug of mesalamine acting locally on colonic mucosa, blocking production of arachidonic acid metabolites.
medtap_lines.Becaplermin: Recombinant platelet-derived growth factor, driving chemotaxis and proliferation of cells involved in wound repair.
medtap_lines.Belinostat: Histone deacetylase inhibitor, causing accumulation of acetylated histones at nanomolar concentrations.
medtap_lines.Bexarotene: Selectively binds and activates the retinoid X receptors RXR-alpha, RXR-beta and RXR-gamma, which act as transcription factors.
medtap_lines.Bicalutamide: Non-steroidal androgen receptor inhibitor, competitively binding cytosolic androgen receptors in target tissue.
medtap_lines.Bivalirudin: Reversibly inhibits thrombin by binding both its catalytic site and its anion-binding exosite.
medtap_lines.Botulinum Toxin Type A: Cleaves SNAP25 inside peripheral cholinergic nerve endings, blocking acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction.
medtap_lines.Bupropion: Weak inhibitor of the neuronal reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine.
medtap_lines.Busulfan: Bifunctional alkylating agent that hydrolyzes to reactive carbonium ions which alkylate DNA.
medtap_lines.Celecoxib: Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis primarily through cyclooxygenase-2, sparing cyclooxygenase-1 at concentrations reached in humans.
medtap_lines.Cilastatin: Renal dehydropeptidase inhibitor that limits the renal metabolism of imipenem.
medtap_lines.clomiphene: Competes with estrogen for estrogen-receptor binding sites, raising the release of pituitary gonadotropins.
medtap_lines.Clonidine: Alpha-2 adrenoceptor agonist acting presynaptically and postjunctionally in the spinal cord on pain signal transmission.
medtap_lines.Darifenacin: Competitive muscarinic antagonist with 9- to 59-fold greater affinity for M3 than for other muscarinic subtypes.
medtap_lines.Decitabine: Incorporates into DNA after phosphorylation and inhibits DNA methyltransferase, causing DNA hypomethylation.
medtap_lines.deferiprone: Chelating agent binding ferric iron in neutral 3:1 complexes stable across a wide pH range.
medtap_lines.defibrotide sodium: Enhances plasmin's hydrolysis of fibrin clots and raises endothelial t-PA and thrombomodulin expression.
medtap_lines.desirudin: Direct inhibitor of free and clot-bound thrombin, one molecule binding one thrombin molecule.
medtap_lines.Dexmedetomidine: Relatively selective alpha-2 adrenergic receptor agonist with sedative properties.
medtap_lines.diclofenac: Inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2, lowering prostaglandin synthesis in peripheral tissues.
medtap_lines.Eliglustat: Specific inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase (IC50 = 10 ng/mL).
medtap_lines.enalapril: Hydrolyzed to enalaprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme and lowers plasma angiotensin II and aldosterone.
medtap_lines.Epoprostenol: Directly dilates pulmonary and systemic arterial vascular beds and inhibits platelet aggregation.
medtap_lines.Eptifibatide: Reversibly blocks platelet GP IIb/IIIa, keeping fibrinogen and von Willebrand factor from binding.
medtap_lines.estrogens, conjugated: Estrogens bind nuclear estrogen receptors in estrogen-responsive tissues.
medtap_lines.Everolimus: Binds FKBP-12 to form a complex that inhibits mTOR, blocking p70S6K phosphorylation and cell proliferation.
medtap_lines.evolocumab: Monoclonal IgG2 that binds PCSK9 and blocks PCSK9-mediated degradation of the LDL receptor.
medtap_lines.Fluocinolone Acetonide: Corticosteroid that induces lipocortins, inhibiting phospholipase A2 and the release of arachidonic acid.
medtap_lines.Fluorouracil: Converted to FdUMP, FUTP and FdUTP, inhibiting thymidylate synthase and incorporating into RNA and DNA.
medtap_lines.Galsulfase: Recombinant N-acetylgalactosamine 4-sulfatase taken into lysosomes by mannose-6-phosphate receptors to catabolize dermatan sulfate.
medtap_lines.Granisetron: Selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist with little affinity for other serotonin, adrenergic, dopamine or histamine receptors.
medtap_lines.heparin: Binds antithrombin III to enhance its serine protease activity, inactivating coagulation factors Xa and IIa.
medtap_lines.hyaluronidase: Hydrolyzes hyaluronic acid at the glucosaminidic bond, lowering the viscosity of connective tissue.
medtap_lines.hydromorphone: Full opioid agonist relatively selective for the mu-opioid receptor.
medtap_lines.Idarubicin: DNA-intercalating anthracycline that inhibits nucleic acid synthesis and interacts with topoisomerase II.
medtap_lines.ifosfamide: Prodrug activated by hepatic cytochrome P450 to isophosphoramide mustard, which crosslinks DNA at guanine N-7.
medtap_lines.Irinotecan: Irinotecan and its metabolite SN-38 bind the topoisomerase I-DNA complex, blocking religation of single-strand breaks.
medtap_lines.Ivacaftor: Potentiator of the CFTR chloride channel, raising its open probability at the epithelial cell surface.
medtap_lines.Lamotrigine: Proposed to act on neuronal voltage-gated sodium channels.
medtap_lines.Lenalidomide: Binds cereblon in a cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, targeting Aiolos, Ikaros and CK1-alpha for degradation.
medtap_lines.Levonorgestrel: Progestin that suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus and alters the endometrium.
medtap_lines.Memantine: Low-to-moderate affinity uncompetitive open-channel NMDA receptor antagonist.
medtap_lines.Mesalazine: Acts locally on intestinal mucosa, blocking production of cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase arachidonic acid metabolites.
medtap_lines.Methadone: Mu-opioid receptor agonist that also antagonizes the NMDA receptor.
medtap_lines.Miglitol: Reversible inhibitor of membrane-bound intestinal alpha-glucosidase enzymes, slowing hydrolysis of oligosaccharides to glucose.
medtap_lines.Miglustat: Competitive reversible inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase, lowering glycosphingolipid synthesis.
medtap_lines.Mitotane: Adrenal cytotoxic agent that modifies peripheral steroid metabolism and directly suppresses the adrenal cortex.
medtap_lines.Morphine: Full opioid agonist relatively selective for the mu-opioid receptor.
medtap_lines.Nelarabine: Prodrug converted to ara-GTP, which incorporates into DNA and inhibits DNA synthesis.
medtap_lines.niraparib: Inhibitor of the poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase enzymes PARP-1 and PARP-2, raising formation of PARP-DNA complexes.
medtap_lines.Norethisterone: Progestin that suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus, lowers the midcycle LH and FSH peaks, and alters the endometrium.
medtap_lines.Norgestimate: Progestin that suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus and alters the endometrium.
medtap_lines.pancrelipase/pancrelipase/pancrelipase: Pancreatic lipases, proteases and amylases hydrolyzing fats, protein and starch in the duodenum and proximal small intestine.
medtap_lines.Paricalcitol: Vitamin D analog binding the vitamin D receptor, inhibiting parathyroid hormone synthesis and secretion.
medtap_lines.Phentermine: Sympathomimetic amine with pharmacologic activity similar to amphetamine.
medtap_lines.Phentolamine: Produces a short-duration alpha-adrenergic block, relaxing vascular smooth muscle.
medtap_lines.progesterone: Steroid that transforms a proliferative endometrium into a secretory endometrium in the presence of estrogen.
medtap_lines.Quinidine: Depresses the rapid inward sodium current in cardiac muscle and Purkinje fibers, slowing conduction and reducing automaticity.
medtap_lines.Rasburicase: Catalyzes enzymatic oxidation of uric acid to the more soluble metabolite allantoin.
medtap_lines.Remifentanil: Mu-opioid receptor agonist rapidly hydrolyzed by nonspecific blood and tissue esterases.
medtap_lines.Ribavirin: May act as an analog of the cellular metabolites guanosine and xanthosine.
medtap_lines.Rifabutin: Inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase in susceptible bacterial strains.
medtap_lines.RK-0202: Acetylcysteine maintains or restores hepatic glutathione and acts as an alternate conjugation substrate for acetaminophen's reactive metabolite.
medtap_lines.Rotigotine: Non-ergoline dopamine agonist stimulating dopamine receptors within the caudate-putamen.
medtap_lines.Scopolamine: Belladonna alkaloid acting as a competitive inhibitor at postganglionic muscarinic acetylcholine receptor sites.
medtap_lines.sebelipase alfa: Recombinant lysosomal acid lipase that breaks down lysosomal cholesteryl esters and triglycerides.
medtap_lines.Somatropin recombinant: Growth hormone acting at growth hormone receptors directly and through local or systemic IGF-1.
medtap_lines.Sugammadex: Modified gamma cyclodextrin that complexes rocuronium and vecuronium, lowering the amount free to bind nicotinic cholinergic receptors.
medtap_lines.technetium tc-99m sestamibi: Cationic technetium complex retained within myocardial mitochondria through electrostatic interactions.
medtap_lines.Tenofovir: Phosphorylated to tenofovir diphosphate, which inhibits HIV-1 and HBV reverse transcriptase and terminates the DNA chain.
medtap_lines.tetrofosmin: Lipophilic cationic complex that diffuses through the cell membrane and is retained by intact mitochondria.
medtap_lines.Tocilizumab: Binds soluble and membrane-bound IL-6 receptors, inhibiting IL-6-mediated signaling.
medtap_lines.Tolbutamide: Stimulates the release of insulin from pancreatic beta cells.
medtap_lines.Topotecan: Binds the topoisomerase I-DNA complex and blocks religation of single-strand DNA breaks.
medtap_lines.Travoprost: Selective FP prostanoid receptor agonist believed to raise uveoscleral outflow.
medtap_lines.Trimethobenzamide: Thought to act at the chemoreceptor trigger zone in the medulla oblongata.
medtap_lines.Urofollitropin: Follicle-stimulating hormone preparation that drives ovarian follicular growth and maturation.
medtap_lines.Valproic Acid: Thought to act by raising brain concentrations of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
medtap_lines.Verteporfin: Light-activated porphyrin generating singlet oxygen and oxygen radicals that damage neovascular endothelium and occlude vessels.
medtap_lines.Vorapaxar: Reversible antagonist of the platelet protease-activated receptor-1, blocking thrombin-induced platelet aggregation.
medtap_lines.Zoledronic acid: Bisphosphonate binding mineralized bone and inhibiting the osteoclast enzyme farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase.

_overrides_comment: Replacement prose for a `mechanisms_summary` row whose source Piru cannot edit, keyed by Piru canonical substance name. The pharmacology of the source row is preserved and only the claim is cut, so these stay paragraphs rather than one-sentence lines; claim_language.py holds them to the medical-claim vocabulary.

overrides.Ariadne:
The psychedelic effects of 4C-D are believed to arise from its activity as a partial agonist at 5-HT receptors. The precise role of these interactions, and the exact mechanism by which they produce a psychedelic experience, has not yet been fully elucidated.

In a forum discussion, users have proposed that 4C-D may function as a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), based on its structural resemblance to 5-MeO-7-Me-AET or 7-Me-AET, the latter of which has been demonstrated to be a potent MAOI and serotonin releasing agent. No evidence supports this property for 4C-D.
overrides.Loperamide:
Loperamide is an opioid receptor agonist that acts on μ-opioid receptors in the myenteric plexus of the large intestine. Loperamide works similarly to morphine, reducing the activity of the myenteric plexus and thereby reducing the tone of the longitudinal and circular smooth muscle of the intestinal wall. It is considered to have low abuse potential due to its significant first-pass metabolism and P-glycoprotein-mediated efflux at the level of the blood-brain barrier. At ordinary oral exposures, low bioavailability and minimal CNS penetration keep central nervous system opioid effects from appearing; they do occur at far higher oral exposures.

Co-administration of P-glycoprotein inhibitors such as quinidine may allow loperamide to cross the blood-brain barrier and produce central morphine-like effects. Studies have found that loperamide combined with quinidine produces respiratory depression, indicating its central opioid action.

Loperamide is metabolized through the cytochrome P450 (CYP) system and is a substrate of the CYP3A4 isoenzyme. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase loperamide concentrations.
overrides.Olanzapine: Olanzapine antagonizes dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, with additional antagonism at histamine H1, muscarinic acetylcholine, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors. Its H1 and muscarinic activity accounts for sedation and dry mouth, and its H1 and 5-HT2C activity for appetite and weight change. Compared with typical antipsychotics it produces less extrapyramidal motor disturbance and less tardive dyskinesia.
overrides.Phenibut:
Phenibut has a more complex pharmacological profile than many other depressants. Unlike benzodiazepines, phenibut acts as a full agonist at GABAB receptors, similar to baclofen and high-dose GHB. At higher doses, phenibut loses its selectivity for GABAB and gains additional activity as a GABAA agonist. Phenibut's action at GABAB receptors is responsible for its sedative effects.

Recent research has shown that phenibut binds to and blocks voltage-dependent calcium channels (VDCCs) containing alpha-2-delta subunits, analogously to gabapentinoid drugs such as gabapentin and pregabalin. Both enantiomers of phenibut exhibit this action with similar potency. The R-enantiomer displays fivefold greater affinity for alpha-2-delta-containing voltage-gated calcium channels relative to GABAB receptors, while the S-enantiomer has no activity at GABAB receptors.

The analgesic effects of phenibut in rodents are mediated not by GABAB receptors but by blockade of voltage-gated calcium channels containing alpha-2-delta subunits.
overrides.Pyrazolam:
Benzodiazepines produce their effects by binding to the benzodiazepine receptor site and acting on γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors, thereby amplifying the efficiency and potency of the neurotransmitter GABA. Because this site is the most prolific inhibitory receptor complex in the brain, its modulation accounts for the sedative (or depressant) effects of pyrazolam on the nervous system.

The anticonvulsant properties of benzodiazepines may be attributable in part or in full to binding at voltage-dependent sodium channels rather than at benzodiazepine receptors.

Pyrazolam is most selective for the α2 and α3 receptor subtypes. It is excreted unchanged and therefore does not interact with hepatic enzymes in the way other benzodiazepines do.

Pyrazolam is structurally similar to alprazolam and bromazepam. Unlike most benzodiazepines, pyrazolam does not appear to undergo metabolism and is instead excreted unchanged in urine.
overrides.Yohimbine:
Yohimbine's primary and most well-studied mechanism of action is antagonism of a class of receptors known as alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, thereby elevating norepinephrine release by blocking the presynaptic autoreceptors that normally damp it. Blockade of alpha-2 adrenergic receptors raises blood pressure, releases insulin, and lowers blood glucose levels. Yohimbine also blocks alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, albeit with lower affinity. Research has additionally shown that it weakly inhibits monoamine oxidase.

At higher concentrations, yohimbine acts as an antagonist at dopamine D2 and D3 receptors, serotonin 5-HT1A, 5-HT1B, and 5-HT2A receptors, and as a partial agonist at 5-HT1A receptors.
overrides.萘哌甲酯: Methylnaphthidate is believed to act primarily as a monoamine triple reuptake inhibitor—that is, it binds to and partially blocks the transporter proteins normally responsible for clearing dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin from the synaptic cleft, raising levels of these neurotransmitters throughout the brain and central nervous system. This leads to an accumulation of these molecules in the brain, particularly within reward pathways, producing stimulant and euphoric effects.
